summary: A yes/no question is the statement with هَلْ in front and the Arabic question mark ؟ at the end; the word order does not change and there is no auxiliary: تُحِبُّ الْجَزَرَ → هَلْ تُحِبُّ الْجَزَرَ؟. The prefix أَ is a more formal alternative and is required before a negation (أَلَا تُحِبُّ …؟ أَلَيْسَ …؟). Answers: نَعَمْ (yes), لَا (no); بَلَى is “yes (on the contrary)” to a negative question.

askYourself: Is it a yes/no question (not who/what/where)? → هَلْ + the unchanged statement + ؟
Does the next word start with al-? → هَلْ takes a helping vowel: هَلِ الْجَزَرَةُ هُنَا؟
Is the question negative? → use أَ, not هَلْ: أَلَيْسَ …؟
Did I write the Arabic question mark ؟ ?

traps: No inversion and no “do”: هَلْ تُرِيدُ جَزَرَةً؟ = do you want a carrot?
Do not combine هَلْ with a question word: *هَلْ أَيْنَ …؟
Spoken Arabic often drops هَلْ and relies on intonation; in writing keep it.
To a negative question, “yes, it is” is بَلَى, not نَعَمْ.

seeAlso.note: Hebrew marks a yes/no question with הַאִם in writing or only with intonation in speech — the same idea as هَلْ.
German moves the verb to the front (Bist du müde?); Arabic never changes the order, it adds هَلْ.
Chinese adds 吗 at the end of the sentence where Arabic puts هَلْ at the start.
